authorship: current assistant semantic reading; program only transports authored decisions

rows.statement: Receive and respond to recruiter emails during job applications.
rows.rationale: Current recruiting communication intent is explicit; later frequent checking confirms its importance.

rows.statement: Receive school notifications and communicate about school matters.
rows.rationale: The primary-use explanation supports this separate communication purpose.

rows.statement: Review unread emails to identify important messages.
rows.rationale: The workflow is intentional triage, not a requirement to reread all mail forever.

rows.statement: Mark important emails for attention.
rows.rationale: A distinct triage action selected by the stakeholder.

rows.statement: Delete unwanted or spam emails to keep the inbox clear.
rows.rationale: This directly combines deletion with its stated organizing purpose.

rows.statement: Read important emails.
rows.rationale: Explicit intended action after initial triage.

rows.statement: Tag emails needing later action so the task can be completed when available.
rows.rationale: Tagging is the chosen means; deferral is not omission of the task.

rows.statement: Delete even important emails once their conversation has ended.
rows.rationale: The condition differentiates this from discarding active important messages.

rows.statement: Separate important recruiting or school messages from deal mail using different email accounts.
rows.rationale: The selected organization strategy is retained without making it the only solution for everyone.

rows.statement: Use an AI assistant to compose an email from the sender's main points, then adjust the draft.
rows.rationale: AI drafting is explicit; internal integration is separately requested later.

rows.statement: Adjust font size when preparing an email.
rows.rationale: A selected composition capability, not a new automatic-style rule.

rows.statement: Make important sentences bold before sending an email.
rows.rationale: Explicit emphasis strategy.

rows.statement: Send the prepared email.
rows.rationale: The direct result is explicit after composition and formatting.

rows.statement: Share multimedia through cloud links so recipients can view it on phones or laptops.
rows.rationale: Preferred strategy when multimedia is sent; not a demand for embedded media or frequent attachments.

rows.statement: Avoid missing important messages due to spam classification, even at the cost of receiving some spam.
rows.rationale: The explicit tradeoff prevents a false goal of blocking all spam.

rows.statement: Edit a sent email rather than sending a separate correction.
rows.rationale: The proposed feature is explicit beyond the reported short undo window.

rows.statement: Let recipients view the current edited email and optionally inspect its editing history.
rows.rationale: Distinct visibility result; both versions remain accessible by choice.

rows.statement: Reliably receive expected emails such as website-registration messages.
rows.rationale: The stated delivery obstacle supports an inferred outcome; no transport cause is invented.

rows.statement: Compose a well-organized email from brief input using an assistant built into the email client.
rows.rationale: A distinct explicit integration request, preserving the selected in-client mechanism.

rows.statement: Warn before sending when the text says an attachment is present but the file is missing.
rows.rationale: The existing feature is explicitly valued and should be preserved, not discarded as mere fact.

rows.statement: Use AI to extract the main points of received emails.
rows.rationale: Explicit request confirmed as summarization.

rows.statement: Highlight important keywords or details so the reader does not overlook them.
rows.rationale: The assessment example explains the separate highlighting outcome.

rows.statement: Avoid missing messages from recruiting teams.
rows.rationale: Frequent checking is expressly motivated by this avoidance result; checking count is not a service frequency requirement.

rows.statement: Reduce the time spent reading every email.
rows.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly identifies the routine task to simplify.

rows.statement: Consider periodic summaries of batches of received emails as one way to reduce reading effort.
rows.rationale: The interviewer suggestion receives tentative acceptance as one possible solution, not a mandatory three-email schedule.

rows.statement: Receive notifications for important messages if importance detection is sufficiently reliable.
rows.rationale: The speaker declines full reliance if important messages may be missed; conditional strength retained.

rows.statement: Forward email when coordinating work under a tight deadline.
rows.rationale: A condition-specific existing feature the stakeholder calls important.

rows.statement: Send a message to the whole group using bulk addressing or BCC under a tight deadline.
rows.rationale: The follow-up confirms reaching many people quickly; no privacy interpretation of BCC is invented.

rows.statement: Search emails as an essential daily capability.
rows.rationale: The priority ranking supplies explicit continuing intent.

rows.statement: Filter messages by tags, including through search.
rows.rationale: The speaker considers this achievable through search, not an independent mandatory implementation.

rows.statement: Schedule emails for different sending times.
rows.rationale: The requested ranking places this after searching; it does not make it obligatory or time-specific.

rows.statement: Explore shared, self-defined email categories or protocol identifiers so correspondents can communicate using matching categories.
rows.rationale: An explicitly tentative future proposal, with recruiting as an example and practicality uncertain.

rows.statement: Maintain professional communication with people inside or outside one's employer.
rows.rationale: The future-use intent is explicit and broader than internal communication.

boundary_candidates: The respondent sends no confidential mail; do not infer that security is unimportant to every user or invent a privacy specification.
Rare crashes are a positive current fact without a separate explicit reliability target.
Historical uncertainty about pre-email communication is not a new-client requirement.
